passes.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT TARGET: supplied panoramic terminal hall image. Produce ONE edited panoramic image, EXACTLY the same 3:1 composition and camera/perspective. This is a furnishing/art-direction pass BEFORE layer extraction, not a new building or new shot.

USER'S GOAL: make this grand once-prestigious government TIME-TRAVEL STATION read as a working grand train terminal, through grounded SCI-FI, CYBERPUNK and RETRO-FUTURIST passenger equipment and station decoration. There are no trains; the five empty portal rings are the departure platforms. Bureaucratic civilization has advanced technology in repaired old hardware. Believable function, worn civic grandeur, welcoming institutional surface with controlled/oppressive undertone. Anime-background stylization, clean softly edged readable shapes, broad quiet color fields, selective fine functional detail. No photographic rendering.

PRESERVE all architectural perspective, same eye level, floor geometry, stair/lift positions, bridge, blank overhead departure board, left panoramic windows and extended view, existing continuous locker bank, rear pair of lower portals aligned symmetrically and the forward portal on its own base, the two set-back upstairs portals, lower-right corridor entrances and artifact displays. Leave the city view unchanged as an exterior placeholder for later extraction. DO NOT change leftmost 24 percent of this image: left windows, city, railing and lockers must stay exactly registered to the adjoining panorama. Do not crop or zoom. Do not add more pillars or elevators or turn doorways into displays.

FURNISHING DESIGN, additions kept subordinate to portal silhouettes and spacious terminal:
1. At the LOWER RIGHT side of the hall, create a coherent compact passenger-services area beside the right circulation lane, set back against available wall/pier space. A pair of human-sized slightly rounded industrial ticket/identity-validation terminals, integrated CRT screens dark/off, chunky physical controls, paper/receipt slots, a magnetic card slot, bolted plinths, utilitarian cable routing down into the floor. One warm ochre enamel housing and one pale warm-gray service housing with charcoal trim. No free-floating holograms. Keep portals and entrances accessible, at least a generous 2-person walking lane.
2. A modest station waiting area at the right foreground edge, attached modular metal seating with oxblood vinyl pads, coherent human scale, scuffed metal legs standing on the floor. A narrow utilitarian vending/dispensing machine and wall-mounted public communication handset nearby, each with a legible purpose and practical maintenance panels. A battered refuse sorting bin at the end of the seats. Do not block the existing painting, astrolabe or bust.
3. Upstairs at the back/right perimeter, add sparse terminal service consoles, a compact bench and a wall-mounted intercom/first-aid cabinet, integrated with the existing concrete bays. Keep the skybridge continuous and both upper portals well behind the railing with an empty pedestrian aisle in front. NO furniture or cabinets in the bridge's route.
4. Add a few grounded time-travel infrastructure details: rectangular power/cooling modules attached low beside portal bases, protected utility conduits along EXISTING wall/ceiling lines, recessed technical panels. Existing rings remain empty with no energy, glow or visual effects. Infrastructure must connect to actual surfaces and stay out of portal openings.
5. Station civic decoration: retain the existing single painting and museum objects with dusty cases and tarnished plaques; retain blank fabric banners as textile civic accents, no new slogans or flag logos. Replace visual emptiness with useful mechanical details rather than decorative cables everywhere. Analog-looking clock housing with a plain blank insert for later gameplay artwork, only if a sensible supported placement exists.
6. Believable neglect: chipped enamel at handles/corners, seat wear, repaired panel patches, grime around vents, curled blank notice sheets mounted together in a small noticeboard, paper litter collected at wall edges and near bins, dented waste bins. Main circulation remains physically usable. Do not coat everything in noisy damage or scatter valuable artifacts on the floor.

COLOR: material-based variety. Keep worn pale stone and concrete architecture. Hardware in separate restrained accents of warm ochre enamel, muted rust/coral, oxblood upholstery, charcoal, aluminum, dark brown, small worn brass accents. Avoid monochrome blue or green or beige; no green wall, no new green equipment. No neon flood or city-sign cliché. Preserve differing natural materials.

LIGHTING: neutral diffuse base artwork for future dynamic Unity lighting. NO baked directional sunlight streaks, NO lamp pools, NO glowing CRTs or lamps, NO volumetric beams, NO bloom, NO new cast long shadows or nighttime grading. Fixtures/screens dark/off with separate readable lenses. Retain only restrained local form shading/contact cues that communicate shape, not directional scene illumination.
TEXT: no letters, words, numbers, brand names, destination labels, invented signage text or garbled glyphs. Physical blank sign faces, blank screens. Simple safety pictograms may remain. Gameplay supplies text later.
NO people, crowds, desk, desk props, trains, floor-level barricade, obstructed walkways, floating furniture, giant benches, inappropriate suitcases/trolley pile, perspective changes, new window pillars or new architecture.
The result must look like ONE cohesive thoughtfully furnished painted terminal, not objects pasted over the original. Preserve crispness across the full frame.
